answer: Sybil resistance hinges on hardware-backed identities where each AI agent needs a unique cryptographic key attested by a trusted execution environment on specialized, scarce hardware. A computational plume uniquely identifies each agent's processing. To launch a Sybil attack, an adversary must acquire and operate an equivalent number of these ferrous physical devices, incurring immense capital and operational expenses. This ensures that with the dawn of each new agent identity, a significant, verifiable cost is imposed.
